name: IPMT
description: IPMT calculates the interest portion of a payment for a specific period of a loan or investment.
tldr: Finds the interest portion of a loan payment in a given period.

parameters.name: per
parameters.description: The period for which to calculate interest (1 to nper).

parameters.name: fv
parameters.description: Future value or desired cash balance after the last payment (default 0).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: 0 = end of period (default), 1 = beginning of period.

basicExample.description: Interest portion of the first payment on a loan
basicExample.explanation: For a $300,000 loan at 5% annual interest over 30 years, the first month's interest is $1,250.

advancedExamples.title: Interest in a later period
advancedExamples.explanation: The interest portion decreases as the principal is paid down.

howItWorks: IPMT calculates the interest due in a specific period based on the outstanding principal at the start of that period. The result is negative because it represents a cash outflow.

howToSteps.name: Enter rate
howToSteps.text: Use the periodic interest rate (annual rate divided by periods per year).

howToSteps.name: Enter period
howToSteps.text: Choose the period number to analyze.

howToSteps.name: Enter total periods
howToSteps.text: Type the total number of payments.

howToSteps.name: Enter present value
howToSteps.text: Input the loan amount or principal.

limitations: Returns negative values by default because payments are outflows.
Requires consistent period units for rate, nper, and per.
Does not include fees or taxes.

commonErrors.cause: per is less than 1 or greater than nper.
commonErrors.fix: Ensure per is between 1 and nper inclusive.

commonErrors.cause: The result is negative when expecting positive.
commonErrors.fix: Multiply by -1 or use ABS if you need a positive value.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: IPMT works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: What is the difference between IPMT and PPMT?
faq.answer: IPMT returns the interest portion of a payment. PPMT returns the principal portion.

faq.question: Why is IPMT negative?
faq.answer: It represents a cash outflow. Use -IPMT or ABS to show a positive value.

faq.question: Can IPMT calculate cumulative interest?
faq.answer: Sum IPMT over multiple periods or use CUMIPMT.
